messages:
incident-bot: PAGED: High geo-DNS error rate detected for prod-edge (region: EU-west). Alert: 502/503s upstream due to resolver failures. PagerDuty: oncall-rotation.

sre-jordan: acked, looking. Are we seeing NXDOMAIN or timeouts?

ops-ellie: seeing lots of resolver timeouts from EU edge probes, also increased latencies to Cloudflare DNS in metrics.

eng-sam: confirming from app logs: spike in downstream errors referencing "dns lookup failed" and transient connect timeouts to model endpoints.

pm-lee: any customer-facing impact? SLAs? Which customers routed via EU?

ops-ellie: preliminary: ~12% of requests from EU regions failing for ~8 minutes, affects hosted inference endpoints in eu-west-1 region. Some retries succeed.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (auto). Severity: S2 (degraded). Runbook: GeoDNS failure -> check resolver path + failover. Link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/geodns-failures

oncall-rotation: oncall handoff: I'm currently primary, handing to sre-jordan to coordinate mitigations.

sre-jordan: I'll take lead. ops-ellie, can you run a few quick dig checks from edge probes and paste results?

ops-ellie: running: 
```
probe-eu-1$ dig +short A api.prod.redwood.com @1.1.1.1

;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Also tried 8.8.8.8: same timeouts.

eng-sam: ran curl from eu-host: `curl -v https://api.prod.redwood.com/health` shows DNS lookup stalled, then timeout.

sre-jordan: this looks like upstream resolver surge / packet-loss to Cloudflare's authoritative resolvers or Route53 records returning inconsistent responses. ops-ellie, can you check Cloudflare status / Route53 change history?

ops-ellie: Cloudflare status shows no global incident. Route53 change logs show no recent edits. But our GeoDNS provider (internal router) has seen high latencies to CF resolver IPs: 162.159.x.x.

eng-sam: adding dns-trace from an affected host: 
```
$ dig +trace api.prod.redwood.com
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> +trace api.prod.redwood.com
... last step returns SERVFAIL from cf-authoritative.example
```

pm-lee: Customer comms: we should prepare a short status update if impact persists >15m. Ops, any temporary mitigations available?

ops-ellie: options: 1) Flip GeoDNS routing to prefer Route53 direct (bypass CF) if we have identical records; 2) Increase TTLs / rely on cached records (not immediate); 3) Push traffic to fallback region (NA) via routing policy.

sre-jordan: Let's do safe mitigation: enable Route53 direct answers for EU (lower risk) by switching GeoDNS policy to route-to-route53 for eu-west. eng-sam, can you validate Route53 has same A/alias records?

eng-sam: verified: Route53 has identical alias records pointing to alb-eu. No pending change. I can update GeoDNS policy via API.

oncall-rotation: manual rollback plan? If API switch fails, we can scale origin retries and increase client-side retry backoff.

sre-jordan: ops-ellie, perform the switch and post the API call/response here. Tag me when done.

ops-ellie: Running change: `POST https://geo.redwood.internal/v1/policies/route?region=eu-west&provider=route53`
Response: 202 Accepted. Change id: changex-3872.

eng-sam: I see change propagating. Running dig now: `dig +short api.prod.redwood.com @1.1.1.1` -> returns 3 IPs from Route53 set.

ops-ellie: traffic metrics show error rate dropping from 12% -> 2% within 60s. Latency normalizing.

pm-lee: preparing status note: "We experienced a DNS resolution issue affecting EU traffic; routing adjusted to fallback provider, most customers recovered. We will follow up with root cause." Drafting now.

incident-bot: Note: automated rollback protection enabled. If error rate rises above 5% in 5m, change will be rolled back.

sre-jordan: continuing monitoring. eng-sam please keep an eye on cache churn and client retries to avoid thundering herd. Also open support ticket with Cloudflare with trace logs.

eng-sam: opened CF ticket #CF-112233 with dig traces and timestamps.

ops-ellie: also opened AWS support ticket for Route53 audit: #AWS-556677.

oncall-rotation: do we need to do any infra changes (scaling) in fallback region? Metrics look stable but watch concurrency.

eng-sam: temporarily increased connection pool to EU ALBs by +20% to handle reroutes. Will rollback after 30m.

pm-lee: status page updated: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2026-042 (note added: "Partial DNS resolution failures in EU; routing switched to Route53; mitigation in progress")

sre-jordan: good. Let's keep thread for at least one hour after all metrics stable. Next steps: 1) collect pcap/traces for CF resolver traffic, 2) postmortem owner ops-ellie, due in 5 days, 3) follow-up comms to customers with RCA.

ops-ellie: collecting probe pcaps now, saving to /incidents/INC-2026-042/pcaps.

eng-sam: rolling back connection pool increase after 25m; traffic stable.

ops-ellie: monitoring shows sustained errors <1% for last 10m. Marking mitigation successful.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-042: mitigated. Time to mitigated: ~14 minutes. Severity downgraded to S3 (informational).

pm-lee: I'll send initial customer follow-up and schedule RCA with ops-ellie and eng-sam.

sre-jordan: thanks team. Handoff to oncall-rotation for post-incident monitoring and follow-up.

oncall-rotation: acked. logging final notes to incident tracker and closing channel in 2h unless new alerts. :white_check_mark:

ops-ellie: final note: need to add play to runbook to automatically failover early when CF resolver packet-loss > 5% to reduce blast radius. Filing PR on runbook now.

eng-sam: added CF ticket updates; will append any provider response to postmortem.

pm-lee: closing comms loop after RCA. Good job. :tada:
